rows.why: He attempted 'aswad' then trailed off; she substituted sayyie' and he built on it (baseer sayyee'). Tier 1 holds, though aswad/aswa2 ambiguity keeps it medium.
Farsi false friend: he used مظلوم for calm/unreactive, she said not the same meaning and supplied رايق/رايقين (53:14). Tier 1 vocab.
He put -هم on يخلص (their work = it); she recast يخلصوه (23:24). Object ending on the verb = D4, plural verb = B18.
He did not catch بيهمنا in her sentence, guessed 'important like muhim'; she explained 'it matters to us'. Didn't-know, tier 0 asked.
Command of doubled-middle verb: he offered echarrab/echarrbi, she hinted, then said No, خرّب (44:55-56) and quizzed the a- drop rule. B10.

Transcript 'أب الامبارح' is phonetically 2abl embare7 = قبل امبارح with ق->ء (S4, urban Levantine); he was only unsure whether it is 'el-mbare7' or 'mbare7'. Her line 'قبل امبارح or أول امبارح some people say' echoes his form and adds a variant, no 'no'; then she carries on. Not a made-up word.
rows.should_be: drop (S4 pronunciation / transliteration artifact, not a vocab miss)

'daiman sos behtr' with no verb; she recast دايماً بيكون صوص... and chat has daymaan beykoon el-sauce bey7re2. B8 habitual ykoon; A1 el- only in chat, fine as bucket2.
من واحد لتنتين; she prompted 'ساعة دايماً feminine', he gave واحدة then الواحدة للتنتين, ممتاز (51:22). E2.

'عملنا كتير' is ordinary Levantine; her 'شو عملنا؟' twice then 'عنجد؟ تعبت؟' reads as end-of-lesson conversation asking what he means, not a grammar correction, and the row itself is low confidence. C9 (word order) does not describe a missing object in any case.
